newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Fresh fighting in Sri Lanka's north kills 45.
newsitem.headline: Fresh fighting in Sri Lanka's north kills 45.

text.p: Sri Lankan troops, slowed by fierce counter-attacks from separatist Tamil rebels, edged forward into northern rebel-held territory on Sunday, the Defence Ministry said.
Troops, who resumed their drive on Saturday after a five-day pause, had advanced three km (1.8 miles) farther north of the former rebel-controlled town of Omanthai, a Defence Ministry statement said.
"Troops advanced into enemy-dominated territory, successfully overcoming heavy terrorist resistance," the statement said.
It said 14 soldiers had been killed and 19 others wounded in Saturday's fighting, adding that no casualties were reported from sporadic rounds of artillery and mortars fired by the rebels overnight.
Ground troops have confirmed more than 30 rebels were killed and more than 75 wounded in the day's fighting, the statement said.
A statement issued by the rebels' international secretariat in London said they had lost only six fighters in fighting since Saturday.
Security sources in the north told Reuters the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas were putting up stiff resistance and slowing the government advance.
Most of Saturday's fighting was concentrated outside Omanthai, they said.

Security forces captured Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of the government-held town of Vavuniya, and Nedunkeni, 40 miles (25 km) northeast of Vavuniya, last week after a two-pronged thrust into the LTTE's northern Wanni heartland.

Some 20,000 troops launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north. Vavuniya lies 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo.
Government forces rely on air and sea links to supply bases and civilians in Jaffna, the LTTE's former would-be homeland brought back under government control one year ago.

The LTTE, fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east, has accused Colombo of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.

Casualty figures released by the Defence Ministry indicated 89 soldiers had died in the 13-day old offensive, one of the military's biggest in the 13-year-old ethnic war. About 145 soldiers had been wounded in the offensive.
Hospital sources said some 600 soldiers were wounded.
The LTTE said the rebel death toll up to Saturday was 65.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war, but the LTTE say the toll is higher.
